1.
This is a claim petition filed under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for grant of compensation.
2. Respondent no. 1 is the driver, Respondent No. 2 is the owner and Respondent No. 3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

3. It is stated in this claim petition that on 20.01.10, at about 7.00 p.m., at L & T Construction Site,
Terminal3, IGI Airport, New Delhi, the claimant was working as a helper with his contractor namely Budha Dev Adak.

Due to negligent driving of the offending vehicle, a crane bearing temporary no. HR99AX5456 and permanent no. HR55G9229, by Respondent No. 1, the claimant was grievously injured and was treated at Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi.

4. It is stated that information of the accident was given at P.S. IGI Airport which was reduced into D.D. Entry No. 23 A dated 20.01.10 and later on it was converted into FIR No. 37/10 registered under Section 279/338 of IPC.
5.
It is stated that a sum of Rs. 8,45,000/ is already incurred on the treatment of the claimant.
This payment has been given by L & T as per policy of the principal employer and would be deducted from the bills of sub contractor.
Therefore, it is prayed that cost of treatment payable to the claimant be given to the sub contractor, Sh. Budha Dev Adak.
6. It is also stated that the claimant was earning Rs. 6,500/ per month and is advised bed rest from the date of accident till the filing of this claim petition.
7. In these circumstances, claimant has claimed a compensation of Rs. 35 lacs from the respondents with interest as applicable from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

8. Respondent No. 1 and 2 have filed a common written statement where they have stated that no such accident as alleged in the claim petition has ever taken place due to any rash and negligent driving of Respondent No. 1.
Respondent No. 3 had insured the vehicle.

Therefore, liability, if any,
to pay the compensation is of Respondent No. 3.

It is also stated that Respondent No. 1 was having a valid driving license to drive the alleged offending vehicle which was seen by Respondent No. 2 prior to employment of Respondent No.

2 1.
Respondent No. 2 had also taken driving test of Respondent No. 1 before employing him as a driver.
Therefore, it was denied that there is any responsibility of Respondent No. 1 and 2 to pay any compensation to the claimant.

9. Insurance company stated in its written statement that before any liability could be fastened upon it, the insured must prove that the driver of special type truck bearing no. HR55G9329 was having a valid and effective driving license, permit and fitness on the date of accident.
Rest of the contents of claim petition were denied but factum of insurance of the offending vehicle on the date of accident was admitted.

10. To decide the compensation payable to the claimant, following issues were framed:
1) Whether, petitioner Baleshwar Munda have sustained injuries on his person in an accident which took place on 20.01.2010 caused due to negligent driving of the vehicle bearing registration number HR55/G9229 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3?
OPP 2) In case, issue no. 1 is decided in affirmative then to what amount of compensation, petitioner is entitled and from whom?
OPP 3) Relief.
11. Claimant filed his evidence by way of affidavit stating similar facts as were already stated by him in the claim petition.
12. In cross examination he admitted that the expenses incurred by him on his treatment were directly paid by his principal employer through contractor.
Other suggestions contrary to his case were denied by him.

13. Claimant examined the Sub Contractor Sh. Budha Dev Adak as PW2 who stated in his evidence by way of affidavit that he is a Sub Contractor with L & T, ECC Division, C/o DIAL at IGI Airport,
New Delhi; he is employer of claimant who was working for him as a helper at a salary of Rs.
6,500/ per month; L & T has paid entire cost of medical treatment of claimant which is approximately Rs. 8,50,000/; he was bearing all other expenses of the claimant during treatment period; claimant was admitted for second operation of his head injury in Rockland Hospital and a sum of Rs. 2,38,053/ were spent on his treatment and the expenses incurred by him as well as L &
T be given to them by the insurance company of the offending vehicle.

14. In cross examination, he stated that he has a work order given by L & T, the principal employer,
but there is no written agreement that expenses incurred by principal employer for the treatment of his employees for injuries suffered by them in the accident while working for principal employer are to be deducted from payments to be given to him by L & T.
He admitted that there is no such clause between him and his employer under which he was to pay back expenses incurred on their treatment by him.
Other suggestions contrary to his examination in chief were denied by him.

Sh. M.L. Verma was examined by the claimant as PW3 who stated that he is working as Manager Industrial Relations in DIAL and L & T has spent Rs. 10,96,000/ on the treatment of the claimant.
He proved medical bills of the treatment of the claimant as Ex. P1.
He stated that L & T has recovered a sum of Rs. 2 lacs from Budha Dev Adak, the Sub Contractor for whom claimant was working at the time of the accident.
He further stated that as and when further payments will become due and payable, balance amount will also to be deducted from that contractor.

He stated that L & T has a tie up with Indian Spinal Injuries Centre and Rockland Hospital whereby payments are given directly by L & T and L & T recovers it from the contractor whose employee is got treated by L & T.
PW3 also stated that there is no written contract in this regard with the contractor.

16. In cross examination, he deposed that claimant was an employee of a sub contractor and he had not brought any documentary evidence with him to show that Rs. 2 lacs were deducted from the account of sub contractor Sh. Budha Dev Adak.

He also stated that they did not serve any notice upon the sub contractor stating therein that L & T is incurring expenses on the treatment of his labourer and would be recovering the same from his future bills.
17. This witness was reexamined on the application of the claimant and he stated that sub contractor Sh. Budha Dev Adak is working for L & T since 2006.
The sub contractor supplies labour and except for work order, no other agreement is signed between L & T and the sub contractor.
He produced the work order as Ex. PW3/3.
He stated that the limit of quantum of work which can be assigned to the sub contractor is mentioned in work order which is Rs. 59 lacs approximately.
He stated that if L & T has to recover any amount from the sub contractor, it can be deducted from payments payable to him.
He denied that it was responsibility of L & T to get the claimant treated for accidental injuries.

He stated that there was an understanding that the cost of treatment shall be recovered from the payments payable to the sub contractor and balance amount towards cost of treatment shall also be deducted from the payments payable to the sub contractor.

18. In cross examination he again stated that there is no written contract containing a clause that expenses incurred by L & T on the treatment of employee of the sub contractor shall be recovered from the payments payable to the sub contractor.
He stated that there is no other agreement between L & T and sub contractor except work order and there is no agreement that L & T will provide safety equipments to the employees of sub contractor.
He admitted that it is not mentioned on the Worker's Bill that deduction of Rs. 2 lacs is towards cost of treatment of the claimant.
He denied a suggestion that it was the duty of L & T to get the employees of sub contractor treated for injuries suffered at the site.
Other suggestions contrary to his examination in chief were also denied by him.

19. Last witness examined by the claimant was Sh. Rakesh Kumar, Medical Record Officer as PW4 who produced discharge summary of claimant at Indian Spinal Injuries Centre which was exhibited as Ex. PW4/1.
20.
On behalf of insurance company two witnesses were examined.
The first witness that was examined was Sh. Harbhajan Singh, Assistant of M/s. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. as R3W1.

He stated in his evidence by way of affidavit that the driving license of Respondent No. 1 was got Present Address vs Sh. Mahinder Kumar (Driver) on 29 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180513475/
4 verified and a report was received from the Investigator that the driving license is fake.
He stated that a notice was sent to the driver as well as owner of the vehicle to produce a valid driving license of the driver of the vehicle.
He stated that although the insured was served with the notice but driver was not served with the notice as notice sent to him came back undelivered with the remarks that address is incomplete.

He stated that insured had allowed the driver to drive the vehicle without a valid driving license and inspite of notice insured has not produced valid driving license of the driver and driver himself has not come to adduce any evidence or to produce his valid driving license.
Therefore, this being a violation of terms and conditions of policy, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured.

On behalf of insurance company, another witness was also examined from the ARTO Office,
Mathura as R3W2.

This witness, Sh. Ravi Karan Singh produced driving license record of DL No.
8173 of the year 2007.

The said license details were exhibited as Ex. R3W2/1.
He deposed that no driving license was issued in favour of Respondent No. 1 from Mathura Licensing Authority.

23. Respondent No. 1 placed on record copy of DL No. 24644/Farukhabad/08 issued on 28.02.08 where endorsement for driving Transport Vehicle was made on 15.04.09 and it was again renewed from 15.04.12 to 14.04.15.

24. Respondent No. 1 sought to summon a witness from Licensing Authority Farukhabad,
Fatehgarh, U.P.

However, instead of coming to this court, a report was sent by that authority directly where it was stated that the license whose record was sought to be summoned by this Tribunal i.e. DL No. 2644/FKD/08 was issued on 23.02.08 for motorcycle and LMV Private.
Thereafter, endorsement for Transport Vehicle was made on 15.04.09 and now the license is valid till 14.04.15.
25. No other witness was examined in this inquiry by any other party.

26. On the basis of pleadings of parties, evidence on record and arguments addressed, issuewise findings are as under:
27.
Burden of proving this issue is on the claimant.

5 28.

For succeeding in a claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, it is for the claimant to prove that the vehicle which caused the accident was being driven rashly and negligently by its driver.
29. This is sine qua non for getting the relief.

30. The claimant has stated in the claim petition that on the date of accident, he had suffered grievous injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by Respondent No. 1.
31.
These allegations are denied by Respondent No. 1 in its written statement.
The claimant has reiterated these allegations of rash and negligent driving against Respondent No. 1 when he entered in the witness box as PW1.

On that date, Respondent No. 1 was present in the Court but he did not cross examine the claimant.
32.
Therefore, allegations of rash and negligent driving have remained unrebutted and unchallenged.
33. Certified copy of chargesheet filed by the Investigating Officer against Respondent No. 1 is available on record.

Investigating Officer had recorded statement of Shri Jagmohan Munda under Section 161 of Cr. P.C. who had stated that on 20.01.2010, around 7:00 p.m., he along with the claimant was working on structural pad for attending Aero bridge.
At that time, the offending vehicle had hit structural pad as a result of which the structural pad fell down resulting in head injuries to the claimant.
He stated that the driver of the offending vehicle had run away after the accident.

Statement of Sh. Jagmohan Munda shows that the offending vehicle was also operating at the place where the claimant was working standing on structural pad but the Crane had hit the structural pad as a result of which the claimant had fallen down from a great height and suffered head injuries.
34.
Therefore, prima facie negligence of Respondent No. 1 is made out.

35. In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Gawhati High Court has observed as under: "In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case.

entities.text: Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In a criminal case in order to have conviction, the matter is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt and in a civil case the matter is to be decided on the basis of preponderance of evidence, but in a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in a civil case.
No doubt before the tribunal there must be some material on the basis of which the tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to be decided for awarding compensation.
But the tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt the nicety of a civil or of a criminal case.
After all, it is a summary inquiry and this is a legislation for the welfare of the society"

36. In the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. MAC APP. No. 375/06 dated 05.07.12, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held as under: "8. In Bimla Devi and Ors. v.

In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

37. In the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pushpa Rana & Ors.: 2009 ACJ 287, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondentsclaimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal (Supra).

sentences.text:
On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in F.I.R No. 955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle; (ii)
criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of chargesheet under Sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of F.I.R., wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down.
There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of the driver."

38. This case was noticed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as Cholamandalam M.S.
General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh: 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 where adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement.

ISSUE NO. 2:
40.

In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. ACJ 2011 (Vol. I), following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims:

7

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. ACJ 2011 (Vol. I)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner.
(ii) Compensation payable in injury   cases is payable under two heads.
They are  pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages.

Pecuniary damages have three sub heads which are : (i) expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) (a) Loss of earning ( and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising of loss of earning during the period of treatment and (b) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (iii) Future medical expenses.

Nonpecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities (and /or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

(iii) In routine personal injury cases compensation is awarded only under heads (i),
(ii)(a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii) (b), (iii) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
41.
Claimant was admitted in Indian Spinal Injuries Centre from 20.01.2010 to 09.03.2010 as a case of right fronto temporo pareital SDH with right optic lession.
He had undergone emergency right frontotemporo parietal craniotomy with evacuation of SDH with right frontal and temporal lobatomy with duroplasty.
Post operative, claimant was very restless.
He was kept intubated and sedated.
He had developed right pupillary dilation and he was diagnosed to have suffered right optic nerve injury with orbital cellulites.
He had undergone redo craniotomy under general anesthesia and bone flap was removed.
Necrosed tissue was also removed.
42. The claimant was also admitted in the Rockland Hospital on 22.07.2010 and was discharged on 03.08.2010.
He had undergone cranioplasty under general anesthesia on 23.07.2010.
43. The affect of injuries was such that the claimant is suffering from 30% permanent visual disability.
44. Therefore, for Pain and Suffering, claimant is awarded a compensation of Rs. 1,00,000/.
45. Admittedly, the cost of treatment is given by L&T. More than Rs. 10,00,000/ were spent on the treatment of the claimant.

8 46.

Counsel for the claimant argued vehemently that this amount be released by passing an award in favour of sub contractor Budha Dev Adak because L&T has given cost of treatment to the hospital but will recover this amount from the payments payable to the subcontractor.

He stated that a sum of Rs. 2,00,000/ is already deducted from the payments of that subcontractor and more than Rs.
8,00,000/ will also be deducted as and when such payments become due and payable to the sub contractor by L & T.
47.

Unfortunately, except for oral evidence of PW3, Shri M.L. Verma, Manager, Industrial Relations,
L&T, there is no other evidence to inspire confidence that the cost of treatment of employees of sub contractor working for L&T is given by L&T but thereafter, that amount is deducted from payments payable to the subcontractor.
It does not inspire confidence that such an important clause is left to be acted upon only on the basis of oral understanding between the parties without its being reduced into writing.
No such agreement has been placed on record to show that the payments given by L&T for treatment of claimant are to be deducted from the payments payable to the subcontractor.
48. On behalf of claimant, only one document is placed on record which is Ex. PW3/1 which is Piece Rate Workers Bill.
This bill as dated 19.07.2009.
As per this, a sum of Rs. 5,78,261/ was released in favour of subcontractor.
This document does not show that unless and until cost of treatment is also awarded in favour of claimant, this amount will be deducted from the payments of sub contractor.

49. It appears that the cost of treatment of the claimant was borne by L & T because L & T being the principal employer is responsible to pay for the treatment of the employees of Sub Contractors working at the sites of L & T.

For this, reliance can be placed on Govind Goyenka v. Dayawati & Ors.,
which is a judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in FAO No. 81/2010 dated 21.03.12.
50.
Therefore, in the opinion of this Tribunal, no relief can be given to the claimant for cost of treatment as the cost of treatment is borne by the principal employer of the claimant.
51. Claimant has suffered 30% permanent visual disability.

This disability certificate was received by the Tribunal directly from DDU Hospital and is therefore admissible in evidence for deciding the compensation payable to the claimant for loss of earning capacity due to permanent disability suffered by him.
52. The 30% disability is visual disability.
This is not functional disability qua entire body of the claimant.
Therefore, permanent functional disability qua entire body shall be taken as 15%.
53. Claimant has stated that he was earning Rs. 6,500/ per month being an employee of Sub Contractor.
However, this assertion is denied by respondents.

Although the employer of the claimant, PW2 also stated that he was paying a sum of Rs. 6,500/ per month to the claimant but in absence of any other supporting evidence in the nature of salary slip etc., the income of the claimant cannot be taken as Rs. 6,500/ per month at the time of accident.

9 54.
Since claimant was working at the site of L & T at IGI Airport, this Tribunal assumes him to be a semi skilled workman whose minimum wages were Rs. 4,119/ per month at the time of accident.
15% of that would be Rs. 617.85.
This is the financial loss which the claimant will suffer due to permanent disability suffered by him.
55. Since claimant is less than 40 years of age, loss of future prospects to an extent of 50% is also to be awarded in his favour.

Thus calculated, the loss for the claimant will be Rs. 926.77 per month or Rs. 11,121/ p.a.
56.

As the claimant was 27 years of age at the time of accident, multiplier of 17 will apply and financial loss due to this disability will be Rs. 1,89,062/.
57.
Therefore, claimant is awarded compensation of Rs. 1,89,062/ towards Loss of Income due to permanent disability.

58. As noticed earlier claimant had remained admitted in Indian Spinal Injuries Centre from 20.01.10 to 09.03.10 and again from 22.07.10 to 03.08.10.
59. Therefore, claimant would have needed help of an attendant at least for a period of 9 months.
It is settled law that even if gratuitous services are rendered by family members to a victim of road traffic accident, even then compensation is to be awarded for attendant's charges.
60. For this, reliance can be placed on Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. v. Lalita: AIR 1981 Delhi 558 and Narayan Bahadur v. Sumeet Gupta and Anr., MAC APP.

sentences.text: 61. Again relying on minimum wages payable to a unskilled workman which on the date of accident were Rs. 3,953/ per month, the claimant is awarded a compensation of Rs. 35,577/ for Attendant's Charges.

62. Considering long treatment of the claimant in the hospital and also considering the seriousness of the injuries suffered by the claimant, claimant is awarded a compensation of Rs. 25,000/ for Special Diet and Rs. 25,000/ for Conveyance Charges.

63. Therefore, total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs. 3,74,639/ which will be paid with interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of this Claim Petition which is 11.05.10 till its realization.
64. Next question is which of the respondents is liable to pay this compensation to the claimant?
65. The driving license seized by the police from Respondent No. 1 was found to be a fake driving license.
This is evident from the testimony of R3W2, Sh. Ravi Karan Singh, Junior Clerk, ARTO Mathura who had stated that DL.No. 8173/07 was issued to Sh. Hukam Singh and not to Respondent No. 1.

10 66.
Insurance company has served a notice upon Respondent No. 1 to produce valid driving license authorising him to drive the offending vehicle on the date of accident.
67. Pursuant to that notice, Respondent No. 1 has filed on record DL. No. 24644/FKD/08.
To begin with, this driving license was issued only for Motorcycle and LMV Private.
However, endorsement for Transport Vehicle was made on 15.04.09 which was effective till 14.04.12.
Therefore, on the date of accident, Respondent No. 1 had a valid driving license.
68. Respondent No. 1 had sought to summon a witness from Licensing Authority, Farukhabad to prove his driving license.

However, a report was received from ARTO (A) Farukhabad (Fatehgarh)
directly addressed to this Tribunal admitting validity of the driving license in question.

69. Once a report is received directly from Licensing Authority by the Claims Tribunal, the same is presumed to be correct and has to be read in evidence without formal proof, till proved to the contrary.

For this, reliance can be placed on Rule 7 of the Delhi Motor Accident's Claims Tribunal Rules, 2008.
70.

sentences.text:
This report is on record since 30.07.13.
71.
Insurance company has not adduced any evidence that the report is not correct or Respondent No. 1 was not having a valid driving license on the date of accident.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a claim petition filed under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for grant of compensation.
Due to negligent driving of the offending vehicle, a crane bearing temporary no. HR99AX5456 and permanent no. HR55G9229, by Respondent No. 1, the claimant was grievously injured and was treated at Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi.
Respondent No. 3 had insured the vehicle.
Therefore, liability, if any,
to pay the compensation is of Respondent No. 3.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
For succeeding in a claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, it is for the claimant to prove that the vehicle which caused the accident was being driven rashly and negligently by its driver.

(i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner.
(ii) Compensation payable in injury   cases is payable under two heads.
They are  pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages.
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii) (b), (iii) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

Therefore, permanent functional disability qua entire body shall be taken as 15%.
Therefore, claimant is awarded compensation of Rs. 1,89,062/ towards Loss of Income due to permanent disability.
